Mariya Takeuchi.bio: Pioneer of 1980s Japanese City Pop whose collaboration with Tatsuro Yamashita defined the nocturnal Tokyo slap-bass and Rhodes synth-funk aesthetic.
Mariya Takeuchi.signature_sound: slap bass, Fender Rhodes, lush brass section, 80s analog synth strings
Mariya Takeuchi.recommended_moments: late-night highway drives, upbeat evening groove, retro 80s nostalgia

Taeko Ohnuki.bio: Acclaimed Japanese singer-songwriter blending jazz-inflected City Pop sophistication with cinematic nocturnal arrangements.
Taeko Ohnuki.signature_sound: warm electric piano, sweeping strings, moody nocturnal synth pads
Taeko Ohnuki.recommended_moments: 4:00 A.M. rainy night reflection, late-night introspection, atmospheric listening

Miki Matsubara.bio: Iconic Japanese City Pop vocalist celebrated for fusing jazz-funk horn sections with soaring melodic hooks.
Miki Matsubara.signature_sound: disco-funk basslines, brass stabs, electric guitar solos, upbeat groove
Miki Matsubara.recommended_moments: energetic night drives, feel-good upbeat sessions, retro party vibes

Yasuha.bio: Japanese City Pop singer-composer renowned for high-tempo slap-bass arrangements and infectious brass-driven hooks.
Yasuha.signature_sound: rapid slap bass, punchy horn stabs, bright clavinet, high-BPM groove
Yasuha.recommended_moments: high-energy cardio workouts, highway driving, upbeat motivation

Anri.bio: Defining voice of summery Japanese City Pop, blending Toshiki Kadomatsu's funk-horn production with breezy coastal melodies.
Anri.signature_sound: horn section stabs, slap bass, synth-brass chords, coastal groove
Anri.recommended_moments: summer drives, upbeat workouts, feel-good nostalgia

Sade Adu.bio: Frontwoman of Sade and the defining voice of sophisti-pop, merging cool jazz saxophone, brushed percussion, and velvet soul-pop.
Sade Adu.signature_sound: tenor saxophone, brushed snare, warm bass, understated electric piano
Sade Adu.recommended_moments: pomodoro study blocks, late-night coding, espresso lounge reading, date night

Grover Washington, Jr..bio: Foundational smooth jazz and soul-jazz saxophonist renowned for warm Fender Rhodes and lyrical horn interplay.
Grover Washington, Jr..signature_sound: soprano and tenor saxophone, Fender Rhodes electric piano, rain-like percussion
Grover Washington, Jr..recommended_moments: Sunday morning coffee, rainy windowpane focus, romantic evening unwinding

Stevie Wonder.bio: Legendary soul, R&B, and synth-pop innovator combining virtuosic synthesizer harmonies with infectious rhythmic bounce.
Stevie Wonder.signature_sound: analog synth leads, harmonica, driving R&B percussion, upbeat hooks
Stevie Wonder.recommended_moments: high-energy cardio workouts, upbeat party sessions, morning motivation

activity_guides.title: Cognitive Flow & Coding Acoustics Guide
activity_guides.insight: Psychoacoustic research shows that tracks between 74–96 BPM with high acoustic warmth (Fender Rhodes, rain foley, and velvet saxophone like Sade Adu's Paradise and Shibuya After Rain) maintain steady cognitive flow during coding and debugging.

activity_guides.title: Night Drive & 80s Japanese City Pop Guide
activity_guides.insight: Steady 105–126 BPM slap-bass grooves and lush Rhodes synth-brass chords (Mariya Takeuchi, Miki Matsubara, Anri) provide rhythmic optic-flow synchronization ideal for nocturnal highway drives.

activity_guides.title: Peak Workout & Upbeat Cadence Guide
activity_guides.insight: Tracks with energy above 0.85 and tempos between 124–136 BPM (Yasuha's Fly-day Chinatown, Stevie Wonder's Part-Time Lover, Billy Ocean's Caribbean Queen) synchronize with running stride cadence.

activity_guides.title: Late-Night Introspection & 4:00 A.M. Guide
activity_guides.insight: Low-valence, atmospheric nocturnal arrangements (Taeko Ohnuki's 4:00 A.M. and Tomoko Aran's Midnight Pretenders) support emotional catharsis and quiet late-night reflection.
